show_hn.story_text:
We’re happy to introduce Artificer, our first robotics decision model for evaluating robot task progress and success.
The problem
Robot systems need feedback during training, evaluation, and deployment. An arm might grasp the right object, but place it in the wrong bin. A robot might’ve only completed part of its task before it stopped. Assessing these outcomes from video often requires manual review or brittle, handcrafted objectives. Though frontier models do well in evaluation, they are expensive and slow. 
Artificer is a 4B parameter model that estimates task completion and progress, at the frontier level, from a task description and video. During deployment, these estimates provide feedback to a robot controller to help decide whether to continue an attempt, retry, or move to the next

Show HN: SnapFire FSR: Full Stack Web Apps Served via Rust IR Engine
show_hn.story_text: SnapFire FSR is a full stack runtime that lets frontend teams write typescript and have it served via Rust. At my current workplace (10M+ DAUs), all we want to do was render composed strings from the backend to a browser using Typescript. Since Node 0.x (went I started with Node), things have changed, freedoms taken away and now security teams recommend to wrap your Node server instance with a sidecar or else your Node project will be blocked. SnapFire FSR changes that for us, no more sidecars. The idea is, you don't need a general purpose VM to compose a web page. Most complex transformations and communications are done by our services anyway. When you need complex computation done without a service then create native Rust functions and call it via Typescript. show_hn.story_text: I built this for my own file-system and CLI workflows. Wherever I notice a friction point, I update this program to address it. For example, when using a cd command to navigate in a terminal, I've made it easy to access ones I've used before, or to find the right directory using a few characters from dir's name. It also smooths over miscellaneous OS-level functionality which I've encountered pain points in.
